label: early copy phase of long sequences, r/g coming up soon
explanation: Almost all activations fall on the first three output steps (the <DEL> step and the next two copy steps, recall_idx 0-2). Those steps hold 96% of activation mass. It essentially never fires during the original phase or late in the copy phase. Activation rate rises with L: L>=7 holds 87% of mass. The rate peaks when 6-8 outputs remain and is highest at recall_idx 1, the step right after <DEL>. Within that window, firing depends on token content. It fires much more when r (next_out lift 7.7x) or g/l will be output within the next few steps, and more when the input is the digit 1. These content preferences are graded, not all-or-none. The early-window/long-L condition alone gives mass recall 0.87 but precision only 0.07. Adding upcoming r/g raises precision to about 0.17 with mass recall about 0.60. Many activations with no upcoming r/g are missed, so the content dependence is only partly captured.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=1 (+2.78), orig3=r (+2.41), orig4=r (+2.36), orig5=r (+1.99), recall_idx=1 (+1.98), orig5=g (+1.95). Lower it: recall_idx=6 (-3.43), orig3=v (-2.97), orig4=v (-2.77), in_tok=r (-2.66).
